question: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: The geographer Luke Howard first documented the urban heat island effect in the city of London during the 1810s and 1820s.

Pavement and buildings absorb heat from the sun during the day and release it only slowly after dark, while tall buildings and narrow streets trap the warm air and block the cooling breezes that might carry it away.
City centers can be several degrees warmer than nearby rural areas, an effect that is especially pronounced after dark.

An urban heat island is a built-up area that stays warmer than the surrounding countryside because pavement and buildings absorb heat by day and release it at night, leaving city centers several degrees warmer, especially after dark.

explanation: The correct answer is D. A reader new to the idea needs both a definition and the reason behind it, and D supplies both: it defines an urban heat island as a built-up area warmer than its surroundings and explains why, noting that the difference is largest after dark. A gives only a historical detail without defining the concept; B lists causes without naming or defining the effect; and C states the result but never explains what an urban heat island is or why it occurs.

studentNotes.intro: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
bullets: An "urban heat island" is a built-up area that stays warmer than the countryside around it.
The geographer Luke Howard documented the effect in London in the 1810s and 1820s.
Pavement and buildings absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night.
Tall buildings and narrow streets also trap warm air and block cooling breezes.
As a result, city centers can be several degrees warmer than nearby rural areas, especially after dark.
studentNotes.goal: The student wants to introduce the concept of an urban heat island to a reader who has never encountered it.
